title: Unique path between vertices in a tree
statement: Let $G$ be a tree on a finite vertex set, and let $u$ and $v$ be any two of its vertices. Then there is exactly one path in $G$ from $u$ to $v$; that is, among all walks from $u$ to $v$, precisely one has no repeated vertices.
replaced:
\emph{In a tree, any two vertices are connected by a unique
path.}
